name: Don Caballero
label: Touch and Go
lede: An instrumental band from Pittsburgh named after an SCTV mob boss, built around a drummer they called the Octopus, that burned through bassists, punched holes in club walls and ended its best line-up in a snowbank on I-75.

eras.title: Named for an SCTV mob boss
eras.text: Three Pittsburgh musicians started jamming in 1991 meaning to find a singer, then got paid gigs before they found one and never bothered. Ian Williams made it two guitars, and Steve Albini recorded the first album.

years.h: Damon Che, Mike Banfield and Pat Morris start Don Caballero
years.p: In Pittsburgh, drummer Damon Che, guitarist Mike Banfield and bassist Pat Morris form an instrumental trio, named after Joe Flaherty's SCTV character Guy Caballero in his Godfather parody as "Don Caballero".
years.xp: They meant to add a vocalist, but early rehearsals turned into paying gigs, so they stayed instrumental. Their 1991 recordings came out in 2014 as Five Pairs of Crazy Pants, Wear 'Em: Early Caballero.

years.h: Ian Williams joins as second guitarist
years.p: [[Ian Williams|6f638f18-7563-4d1f-bc71-b1e2bcad3eff]] joins Don Caballero on guitar. The band's first 7-inches come out that year: the Lucky Father Brown EP on Pop Bus and "Unresolved Karma" on Broken Giraffe.

years.h: For Respect: Don Caballero's Touch and Go debut
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] records Don Caballero's first album for Touch and Go. Bassist Pat Morris leaves after it's released.

eras.title: Rock, not jazz
eras.text: The bass chair became a revolving door, the drums got wilder, and the second album came with a manifesto in the liner notes. Then everyone went off to side projects for two years.

years.h: Three bassists in three years: Jencik, Reid, Draguns
years.p: After Pat Morris leaves, Don Caballero's bass spot passes from Matt Jencik to Dave Reid to George Draguns between 1993 and 1996.

q: Don Caballero is rock not jazz.
years.h: Don Caballero 2 and its liner-note manifesto
years.p: Don Caballero's second Touch and Go album comes with a declaration in the liner notes: the band is rock, not jazz, and free of solos. Songs include "Please Tokio, Please This Is Tokio" and "Rollerblade Success Story".
years.xp: Critic Steve Huey wrote that Damon Che's manic explosions and stop-on-a-dime time changes mapped out the path the guitarists followed. Che's flailing arms earned him the nickname the Octopus.

years.h: Hiatus: Speaking Canaries for Che, Storm & Stress for Williams
years.p: Don Caballero stop for two years. Damon Che plays in [[Speaking Canaries|95f2fde0-0952-4935-854b-ff9faac72f96]] with Karl Hendricks, and Ian Williams forms Storm & Stress with Eric Emm and Kevin Shea. A free live 7-inch comes with Chunklet No. 11.

eras.title: What Burns Never Returns
eras.text: Back with Pat Morris, Don Caballero made the record that math-rock musicians still cite: less distortion, more tapping, more space. Then the line-up shifted again.

years.h: Don Caballero regroup with Pat Morris back on bass
years.p: After two years off, Damon Che, Ian Williams and Mike Banfield reconvene with original bassist Pat Morris.

years.cap: What Burns Never Returns, Touch and Go, 1998
years.h: What Burns Never Returns, the math-rock musician's favorite
years.p: Ian Williams moves to finger-tapping and effects pedals on Don Caballero's third album. Meshuggah's Tomas Haake and Battles' Dave Konopka call it a favorite, and Marnie Stern credits a Don Cab live video for her tapping.

years.h: Pat Morris out, Eric Emm in; Mike Banfield retires
years.p: Storm & Stress bassist Eric Emm replaces Pat Morris, and guitarist Mike Banfield quits later in the year. [[Jon Fine|7af946b0-9715-41ca-a449-e1937e98e69e]] of [[Bitch Magnet|6be97715-b3fe-421b-b478-c4462ee9de15]] fills in on tour.

years.h: Singles Breaking Up (Vol. 1) gathers the 7-inches
years.p: Touch and Go collects Don Caballero's early singles, including "Andandandandandandandand" and "Our Caballero", on one disc.

eras.title: The last tour, the ice, the semi
eras.text: Now a Chicago trio, Don Caballero made its most celebrated album with loop pedals standing in for the missing guitarist. The tour behind it was a slow-motion breakup, and it ended in a crash on the interstate.

years.h: American Don: nine songs, looped at Electrical Audio
years.p: Recorded at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio, Don Caballero's fourth album has Ian Williams and Eric Emm layering parts with Akai Headrush loop pedals to cover for Mike Banfield's absence. Titles include "A Lot of People Tell Me I Have a Fake British Accent".
play: You Drink a Lot of Coffee for a Teenager

years.src: Fred Weaver, 'The Dark Final Days of Don Caballero' (Chunklet / Mycophobia)
years.h: In Atlanta, Damon Che punches four holes in the Eyedrum's walls
years.p: On Don Caballero's fall 2000 tour, a frustrated Damon Che punches four holes in the walls of Atlanta's Eyedrum, which charges $50 a hole, tourmate Fred Weaver wrote.
years.xp:
In Boston, Che refused to play his solo set unless the opening band, Pizza, came off the bill. It did, and Pizza's fans threw slices of pizza and heckled every act all night.

The tour opened in Louisville with Che getting shocked by a microphone and walking off after less than ten minutes.

years.big: "I can't see doing another tour with Ian."
q: I can't see doing another tour with Ian.
years.h: A broken cassette and a front seat end Che and Williams' partnership
years.p: At a gas station near New York, Ian Williams takes Damon Che's front seat while Che is fixing a cassette. Che throws the tape across the lot and says he's done touring with Williams.
years.xp: Tension had built all tour: Williams said the members' solo sets were ruining the band's reputation and the new record, and Che said he couldn't keep touring with him. The band agreed to split after the last date.

years.h: Don Caballero's van crashes on I-75 on the way to the final show
years.p: Driving to the Detroit finale in a whiteout, the van clips a slow Buick, is hit by an 18-wheeler and a jackknifed trailer, and ends up in a gully under an overpass. Everyone survives; the Detroit show never happens.
years.xp: Fred Weaver, driving, said the van's whole left side was crushed. His account, 'The Dark Final Days of Don Caballero', ran in Chunklet.

eras.title: Damon Che's Don Caballero
eras.text: Ian Williams went on to Battles; Damon Che kept the name and rebuilt the band around Pittsburgh's Creta Bourzia. Two Relapse albums, first trips to the UK and Japan, and even vocals followed before it petered out in Spain.

years.h: Ian Williams starts Battles
years.p: Ian Williams forms [[Battles|8522b9b6-b295-48d7-9a10-8618fb80beb8]] in New York. Damon Che plays with Bellini, Eric Emm with Good Morning, Pat Morris with The Poison Arrows.

years.h: Damon Che relaunches Don Caballero with Creta Bourzia
years.p: Damon Che re-forms Don Caballero with Jeff Ellsworth, Gene Doyle and Jason Jouver of Pittsburgh's Creta Bourzia. Mike Banfield and Pat Morris were invited back and said no.

years.h: World Class Listening Problem on Relapse
years.p: Signed to Relapse Records in 2005, the new Don Caballero get mixed reviews and play the UK and Japan for the first time. Jeff Ellsworth leaves in 2006.

years.h: Punkgasm: the only Don Caballero album with singing
years.p: Recorded at Rust Belt Recorders in Royal Oak, Michigan. Damon Che sings on "Dirty Looks", and on the title track he plays guitar while Gene Doyle drums.

years.h: A last Don Caballero show in Spain
years.p: Don Caballero stop after a show in Spain. In 2014 Damon Che told Noisey the band technically still existed as a part-time band.

eras.title: Saving the tapes
eras.text: The archive came out in pieces through Joyful Noise, and Che started a fight against time: master tapes going sticky after thirty years in his care.

years.h: Gang Banged with a Headache, and Live on Joyful Noise
years.p: Joyful Noise Recordings releases a 2003 Don Caballero recording. In 2014 it adds two archival sets of the 1991–92 band.

years.h: Damon Che crowdfunds rescue of Don Caballero's decaying masters
years.p: Damon Che launches a GoFundMe to digitize master tapes he'd kept for 30 years before sticky-shed syndrome ruins them, and starts a YouTube channel of drum covers of the catalog. The campaign hits its goal.

years.h: Damon Che and El Ten Eleven's Kristian Dunn form Yesness
years.p: Damon Che teams with [[El Ten Eleven|6c99afec-a207-4519-9d39-616880b6177b]] bassist Kristian Dunn as Yesness; See You at the Solipsist Convention comes out on Joyful Noise.
